meta.note: Compiled from public defence-news reporting, Wikipedia, and HAL statements available as of Aug 2026. Program timelines in this sector shift frequently -- treat dates as directional, not contractual, and re-verify before citing to a panel.

items.purpose: Indigenous afterburning turbofan for trainers, business jets, and UAVs up to 9 tonnes (twin-engine config)
items.status: Under development; 2 core engines + 1 technology demonstrator built; progress has lagged original 2025 target, now moving toward endurance testing per 2026 tender activity
items.mission: Power source for single-engine trainer jets, business jets, and UAVs up to 5 tonnes (9 tonnes twin-engine)
technology: Indigenous casing/gearbox fabrication (recently outsourced to private industry)
items.platform: Applicable to fixed-wing trainers, UAVs, light jets
items.description: First run December 2015; an internally-funded HAL program (outside formal MoD review), which has contributed to its slower pace versus externally-mandated programs. Potentially relevant to future GARUN-class UAV propulsion if scaled or adapted.

items.purpose: Indigenous turboshaft to replace imported Shakti/Ardiden engines in HAL's helicopter fleet
items.status: 5 prototype engines under fabrication; core achieved 100% RPM milestone; deliveries slated from mid-2025, moving into endurance/certification testing through 2026
items.mission: Powerplant for 3-8 tonne class helicopters (Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand, LUH)
technology: Joint HAL Engine Division (Koraput) / DMRL development
High-altitude cold and hot weather trials completed (Leh, South Pullu, Khardung La)
items.platform: Applicable to Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand, LUH helicopter family
items.description: First run February 2018; positioned as India's path to full engine independence for its indigenous helicopter fleet, reducing reliance on the license-built Shakti/Ardiden engine.

items.purpose: Current-generation turboshaft powering HAL's operational helicopter fleet
items.status: Operational, in service (license-built via HAL/Safran joint venture)
items.mission: Powerplant for Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand, and LUH
items.description: The Safran-designed, HAL-license-built engine that HTSE-1200 is intended to eventually supersede for full indigenization.

items.purpose: Imported turbofan powering the Tejas Mk1/Mk1A fighter fleet
items.status: Operational but a recurring supply-chain bottleneck; delivery delays repeatedly cited as the primary constraint on Tejas Mk1A production rate
technology: Afterburning turbofan, US General Electric design
items.description: Import dependency here is the direct driver behind HAL's indigenous HTFE-25/HTSE-1200 push and the broader 'engine self-reliance' narrative across HAL's current program set.

items.purpose: Higher-thrust turbofan selected for the Tejas Mk2
items.status: Selected/contracted; not yet flight-integrated as Tejas Mk2 prototype assembly is ongoing
items.mission: Powerplant for Tejas Mk2 (Medium Weight Fighter)
technology: Afterburning turbofan, US General Electric design
Transfer-of-technology (ToT) discussions ongoing for future domestic production
items.description: A significantly higher-thrust engine than the F404, enabling the Mk2's larger MTOW (~17.5 tonnes) and expanded payload.

items.purpose: Revived non-afterburning derivative of India's original fighter-engine program, repurposed for unmanned platform propulsion
items.status: Certification targeted late 2026 for the Ghatak UCAV application
items.mission: Propulsion for the DRDO Ghatak stealth UCAV
technology: Developed by DRDO's Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE)
items.description: The original Kaveri program was shelved as a Tejas fighter engine roughly 25 years ago; its revival as an unmanned-platform powerplant is a notable case of programmatic pivot from a failed manned application to a viable unmanned one -- directly relevant precedent for framing GARUN's own propulsion-architecture flexibility.

items.purpose: Future high-thrust engine for AMCA Mk1 and potentially future Tejas Mk2 variants
items.status: Competitive proposal stage; Rolls-Royce has submitted a final proposal offering full IP transfer and core testing by 2030, contingent on a 2026 agreement
items.mission: Powerplant for India's 5th-generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA)
items.platform: AMCA (and potentially future Tejas Mk2 variants)
items.description: Represents the next major decision point in India's engine self-reliance strategy, alongside the indigenous GTRE/DRDO effort.
